changes: Revealed group messages expose a forwarding action through the existing message action descriptor and shared destination modal. Undecryptable content disables forwarding; quarantined/ignored content remains behind the existing gate.

The group source adapter passes only attributed plaintext, original attachment descriptors, file keys and common display identifiers, not source ciphertext as a destination payload. It tracks the selected source object in the current group; replacing/removing that source unmounts the modal and fences late preparation.

The common forwarding source type no longer requires channel/DM-only fields. Encrypted attachment materialization resolves explicit file_key_index or the existing encrypted_N.bin legacy index, preventing a retained attachment after partial upload from using a compacted-array key position. Invalid positions fail rather than guessing another key.
verification: Group component tests cover opening forwarding from revealed content, source replacement closing it, quarantine hiding the action and undecryptable content disabling it. The modal is mocked in these group-source adapter tests.

Forward modal regressions verify explicit and legacy retained index 2 uses key 2 even when it is the only attachment, and an invalid explicit position invokes neither decryption nor destination send. Decryption is mocked; real two-client cryptographic acceptance remains separate.

Focused suites passed: 3 files / 47 tests. Final tsc -b and targeted ESLint passed. Full client suite passed: 229 files / 2210 tests in 45.97s. Vite production web build passed in 740ms. Targeted git diff --check passed; existing warning categories remain visible.
remaining: The source guard intentionally closes on source-object replacement, including non-body updates; finer immutable-version continuity remains a usability improvement. Group source and destination paths still need actual two-client attachment/re-encryption and device acceptance.

Richer DM eligibility/block filtering, revoked-source races outside the group lifecycle and integrated P0-P11 acceptance remain open. No commit, push, merge, server migration, Windows packaging or production release performed.
